newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: McCarthy Retail has tough Q1 - chairman.
newsitem.headline: McCarthy Retail has tough Q1 - chairman.

text.p: McCarthy Retail Ltd said on Wednesday trading conditions in the first quarter of its 1996/97 (July-June) financial year had been highly competitive due to disappointing growth in private consumption expenditure.

Speaking after the annual general meeting on Wednesday, group chairman Brian McCarthy said subsidiary Motor Holdings' had not achieved its budget and its earnings were below those at half year in 1995.

"Whilst Motor Holdings' unit sales are higher than budget and the company has increased its market share, both turnover and gross margins are behind budget due to the continued 'buying down' in both the new and used vehicle markets," he said.
He said a reduction in prices of entry level cars had continued and resulted in further "write downs" of used vehicle stock.
However, Motor Holdings' profits in the second six months of the year were expected to be higher than in the same period in 1995 as stability returned to the market, McCarthy said.
McCarthy Holdings' other main operating subsidiary, Prefcor, had performed well in the first quarter of the year and was well ahead of budget at this stage and well ahead of last year, McCarthy said.

"On the assumption that Prefcor trades in line with budget over the next quarter, their divisions should more than make up any shortfall in McCarthy Motor and thus earnings for the year for the group should be ahead of those achieved last year," he said.
